messages.subject: Multiple Treatments and Mediated Moderation in the same Model
parts:
Hello

Sorry if this question mirrors some earlier questions, but I have not had any luck combining the various answers to the previous questions.  I am still learning Lavaan, so I may well be missing something very obvious. 

I am trying to analyze the results of a 3x2 factorial experiment, where the outcome of interest should be influenced by the interaction between one of the treatments and a mediated variable that is driven by the second treatment)

Specifically , I have treatment 

Exogenous Treatments
X1 (Information)  (two levels)
X2 (Frame)   (three levels)

Mediator
M (Mood)  , influenced by X2

Outcome 
Y(Evaluation) 

The hypothesis I am trying to test is that Y is the result of the interaction between X1 and M, which is in turn driven by X2, so 

Y~X1*M

M~X2

But I am not sure how to properly estimate this model using Lavaan

I have tried to estimate this model in two ways:

a) Use X1 as a grouping factor. This is problematic though, because it doesn't really let me give a good estimator of the marginal effect of moving between the two groups moderated by M

b) Specify an Interaction Term X1*M in advance. But here I am not sure how to code it in such a way that the interaction also captures the fact that X2 has an impact on M

I am probably missing something very obvious, but I would appreciate a pointer on how to best go about fixing this model. 

Thanks!
Chris

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Multiple Treatments and Mediated Moderation in the same Model
parts:
On 07/14/2015 06:00 PM, Chris wrote:
> Y~X1*M

Unlike functions like lm(), lavaan does not use the '*' operator for
specifying interactions.

Since X1 seems to be binary, you can compute the product term 'X1 * M',
and add it to your data.frame (say, myData):

myData$X1M <- myData$X1 * myData$M

Then, you have a new variable 'X1M' in your data, representing the
interaction, and you can write in the lavaan syntax

Y ~ X1 + M + X1M
M ~ X2

Yves.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multiple Treatments and Mediated Moderation in the same Model
parts:
I have tried to estimate this model in two ways:

a) Use X1 as a grouping factor. This is problematic though, because it doesn't really let me give a good estimator of the marginal effect of moving between the two groups moderated by M

Wouldn't the marginal effect of M on Y be estimated by a model with equality constraints on the effect of M on Y across groups (X1)?

Y ~ c(b, b)*M

That model would be nested within the model without the equality constraint, and the chi-squared difference test would be a test of the H0 that interaction == 0.  Assuming you have large enough sample sizes in each group, another advantage of the multiple-groups approach would be that the marginal effect of M on Y from the constrained model could be estimated without assuming homogeneity of error variances across groups, which the use of a dummy variable would have to assume. 

Terry

> Thank you for the response. Just to clarify though: By specifying the
> interaction in advance, how can I ensure that the path model accounts
> for the effect of the second treatment on the "main effect " and on the

>

>
> M~X2 (the effect of the treatment on the main effect)
>
> and
>
> X1M~X2

Hm. The second one is optional, and depends on your theory. Two
alternatives are:

- regress X2 out before you construct the product term X1M
- use a multiple group approach (as Terry suggested).

Yves.
